findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - running land with a sub-minute override, or waiting for remaining jobs after a merge-train check fails.
The full Done-when item also says that new and existing repos get the behavior on upgrade. Land passes `progress=True` (`src/forge/land.py:73`), but `src/forge/checks.py:328` retains each status for 60 seconds. Thus `FORGE_CHECKS_POLL=10` still reads GitHub only once per minute; with `FORGE_CHECKS_WAIT=30`, land can stop even after checks turn green. Separately, the merge-train wait at `src/forge/land.py:700-711` polls `gh pr checks` every 15 seconds regardless of the setting. The coordinator's two-loop ruling did not account for the status cache or this train loop.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - the pull request runs its related tests on Linux.
This override applies only to tests using `fake_clock`. `tests/test_close_pushes_record_after_code_ci.py:20-49` uses neither that fixture nor a polling override, so the new 60-second sleep at `src/forge/checks.py:142` exceeds the command's 60-second timeout in `tests/conftest.py:323-330`. `tests/test_conflicting_pull_requests_stop_check_waits.py:227-244` uses a separate fake clock and still asserts a 15-second sleep. The changed conftest selects these tests for the related run, so they need to be adapted for the new default.
findings.title: Gate: CI wait tests still assume 15-second sleeps

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - closing a previously pushed change while its CI is running, with `FORGE_CHECKS_WAIT=120` and `FORGE_CHECKS_POLL=300`.
The deadline at `src/forge/checks.py:126` is checked only before this full 300-second sleep, so close waits five minutes before checking the two-minute limit. This delays the review-record push beyond the configured wait; the previous 15-second sleep did not cause that delay. Cap this sleep at the remaining deadline, as the final check wait does at line 262.
findings.title: Keep the pre-push wait within its configured deadline

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - closing an already-pushed change or landing with a configured polling interval.
The new proof starts an unpushed fix (`tests/test_land.py:115-127`) and runs standalone close, so `after_code_ci` returns before the pre-push wait (`src/forge/checks.py:156-163`) and land's cached wait is never exercised. Both parametrizations would still pass if the pre-push loop reverted to 15 seconds or land ignored a sub-minute override. The existing pre-push and train tests check ordering or read counts, not polling intervals. Extend the command-boundary proof to cover these paths.
findings.title: Gate: polling interval through pre-push close and land

why: close polls CI checks every 15 seconds, so about 6 closes on one GitHub account use about 4,000 of the 5,000 API requests an hour; a client ran out of quota every hour on 19 Nov 2026 and nothing merged for hours
